title: JANUS Tear Strong 2-SAT Backdoor Policy

definition.strong_backdoor: A variable set B such that every assignment to B simplifies the residual formula to 2-CNF or immediate contradiction.
definition.solver: Enumerate all 2^|B| assignments, solve each residual by implication-graph SCC, and retain one contradiction Tear per rejected branch.
definition.polynomial_condition: k=O(log L) and polynomial-time backdoor discovery

guarded_non_xor_3cnf.construction: (z or a_i or b_i), (not z or c_i or d_i), plus binary block constraints

disjoint_positive_3clauses.construction: m pairwise variable-disjoint positive clauses of width three

tear_format.unsat_branch: two implication paths x->not x and not x->x, or an empty-clause certificate

attack_results.reason: One selector variable reduces arbitrarily many guarded blocks to two 2-SAT instances.

attack_results.target: Every easy CNF has a logarithmic strong 2-SAT backdoor
attack_results.reason: m disjoint positive 3-clauses are trivially SAT but require a backdoor of size m.

attack_results.target: one fixed tractable Tear language is universal
attack_results.reason: The target language must be selected or synthesized adaptively; fixed 2-SAT backdoors can be linear on easy formulas.
Language selection, backdoor discovery, translation verification and witness recovery must all fit one polynomial total-work budget.

sharpened_route.statement: For every CNF F of length L, polynomially select or synthesize a tractable proof language T and find an O(log L) gateway/backdoor or direct certificate into T, with polynomial verification and witness recovery.
sharpened_route.conditional_consequence: Such a construction would decide SAT in polynomial time and prove P=NP.

claim_boundary: This is a parameterized solver and representation-selection attack. It proves neither P=NP nor P!=NP.
